mainTopic: Purity levels and guarding: whether חולין kept at the purity of קודש count as קודש, and when a lapse of attention (היסח הדעת) makes a careful person's items impure
overview: The גמרא first asks whether ordinary food kept at the purity level of קודש counts like קודש. A proof from the silence of the משנה is pushed aside, but the case of יוחנן בן גודגדא shows that it does. Next come rulings that a careful person's clothes become impure through a lapse of attention: a shawl handed back by a friend, and clothes switched by mistake, including a case where רבי עקיבא ruled switched bathhouse clothes impure. רבי אושעיא challenges this with a ברייתא about a barrel guarded as wine that turned out to be oil, which stays pure. To explain that ברייתא, רבי ירמיה says a person can guard an item from impurity but not from being disqualified, and a ברייתא about a basket and a shovel shows that such half-guarding exists. רבה בר אבוה adds stories where רבי ישמעאל praised the rule that intent to guard is what keeps an item pure. The גמרא explains that in the switched-clothes cases the owner truly stopped paying attention. It then asks why a shawl held by a friend should be impure, and רבי יוחנן answers that people do not guard what someone else is holding. The amud ends by questioning that assumption, and the proof comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from the missing level in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier proof: since the משנה lists no separate level for people who eat חולין at the purity of קודש, they must be the same as people who eat קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can prove it from the fact that the משנה does not teach a separate higher level for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an attempted proof that started just before this section. The משנה lists step-by-step levels of purity, and there is no separate step for people who eat חולין at the purity level of קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that if these people had their own level, the משנה would have listed it. Since it does not, the proof concludes they are counted together with the people who eat real קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: A higher level or stricter standard of purity
Ordinary food handled with the purity standard of קודש

phrases.english: From the fact that it does not teach a higher level for them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people who eat ordinary food at the purity level of קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that began before this section
steps.raayaObject: חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש are like קודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The silence of the משנה in חגיגה listing levels of מדרס, which has no separate step for this group

steps.title: Maybe they are like תרומה or like חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe the משנה left this group out because they fit into a level it already lists, either תרומה or חולין, as a תנא holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the reason the משנה gives them no separate level is this: if they are like תרומה, the משנה already taught תרומה, and if they are like חולין, it already taught חולין. As we learned: ordinary food made at the purity of קודש is like ordinary food. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: it is like תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first proof. The silence of the משנה could mean that this group simply fits into a level that is already listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first proof assumed that "no separate level" means "same as קודש." The גמרא shows it could just as easily mean "same as חולין" or "same as תרומה," both of which the משנה already lists. A teaching is quoted where the two opinions are exactly חולין and תרומה, and nobody says קודש. So the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: They are similar to, they are treated like
The כהן's portion of produce, holier than חולין and less holy than קודש

steps.confusionAlert: Neither opinion in the quoted source says this food is like קודש. That is exactly why the first proof is weakened.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא הַאי דְּלָא קָתָנֵי בְּהוּ מַעֲלָה,
phrases.english: But perhaps the reason it does not teach a higher level for them

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי דָּמוּ לִתְרוּמָה — הָא תָּנֵי תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: is that if they are like תרומה, it already taught תרומה,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי דָּמוּ לְחוּלִּין — הָא תָּנֵי לְחוּלִּין.
phrases.english: and if they are like ordinary food, it already taught ordinary food.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: חוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ —
phrases.english: As we learned: ordinary food prepared at the purity level of קודש
is like ordinary food;
רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says:
it is like תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הַאי דְּלָא קָתָנֵי בְּהוּ מַעֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; the question is taken up again with a new proof in step 3
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The silence of the משנה fits just as well with the group being like חולין or like תרומה, and there is a תנאי source holding those very positions

steps.title: New proof from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof from the end of the משנה, about the cloths of יוסי בן יועזר and יוחנן בן גודגדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from the end of the משנה: יוסי בן יועזר was the most pious of the כהנים, and his cloth was treated as מדרס for those eating קודש. יוחנן בן גודגדא ate at the purity level of קודש all his life, and his cloth was treated as מדרס for the purification water.
steps.whatsHappening: The first proof failed, so the גמרא brings a new one from the end of the same משנה. This step quotes the source and sets up the inference that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person's cloth was considered impure only for a level higher than the one he kept. יוחנן בן גודגדא is the key case, because he ate his ordinary food at the purity level of קודש. The next step will show what his case proves.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from the last part (of the משנה)
Impurity as if a זב had sat or leaned on it
Here, the purification water of the פרה אדומה, the highest level of purity
The most pious among the כהנים

phrases.english: Rather, from the last part:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר הָיָה חָסִיד שֶׁבַּכְּהוּנָּה,
phrases.english: יוסי בן יועזר was the most pious of the priesthood,
and his cloth was considered מדרס for קודש.
phrases.notes: In other words, for people eating real קודש, his cloth counted as if a זב had sat on it.

phrases.english: יוחנן בן גודגדא would eat
at the purity level of קודש all his days,
and his cloth was considered מדרס for the חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a new source
steps.raayaObject: חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש are like קודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the משנה about יוחנן בן גודגדא's cloth

steps.title: His care counted for קודש
steps.stepSummary: Since his cloth was impure only for חטאת and not for קודש, the תנא holds that חולין at the purity of קודש are like קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the חטאת, yes; for קודש, no. So he holds that ordinary food prepared at the purity level of קודש is like קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its inference from the case of יוחנן בן גודגדא. Because his cloth was not considered impure for קודש, his practice must have made him pure for קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only the חטאת level for his cloth, which means it was fine for קודש. He only kept his ordinary food at the purity of קודש, so that practice must count as the purity of קודש itself. This shows that, for this תנא, such food is treated like קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The first proof, from the silence of the משנה, failed. The working proof is from יוחנן בן גודגדא: his cloth was impure only for חטאת, so eating חולין at the purity of קודש counts as the purity of קודש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a person's careful purity practice with ordinary food can actually raise his status to the level of קודש.

phrases.english: For the חטאת, yes; for קודש, no.
phrases.notes: Here חטאת means the purification water. His cloth counted as impure for that, but not for קודש.

phrases.english: Apparently, he holds:

phrases.aramaic: חוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת קוֹדֶשׁ כְּקוֹדֶשׁ דָּמוּ.
phrases.english: Ordinary food prepared at the purity level of קודש is like קודש.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַחַטָּאת אִין, לַקּוֹדֶשׁ לָא. אַלְמָא קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the source quoted in step 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the משנה's תנא, חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש are like קודש

steps.title: A fallen shawl handed back by a friend is impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן בן אלעזר rules that if a careful person's shawl falls and a friend hands it back, the shawl is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן בן אלעזר said: if a person's shawl fell off him, and he asked his friend, 'Give it to me,' and the friend gave it to him, the shawl is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about how careful a person must be to keep his clothes pure. Even a short moment of not watching the shawl makes it impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The friend is not said to be impure. The problem is that the owner stopped guarding the shawl for a moment, and that lapse in attention (היסח הדעת) is enough to treat it as impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking one's attention off something; the idea behind this ruling

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar said:
If his shawl fell off of him,
phrases.notes: He means a person who is careful to keep his clothes pure.

phrases.english: and he said to his friend: "Give it to me,"
and he gave it to him, it is impure.
phrases.notes: The friend isn't said to be impure. The owner simply stopped guarding the shawl for a moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the cloths of the careful חכמים from step 3 with new rulings about losing attention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A careful person's shawl that fell and was handed back by a friend is impure, because he stopped guarding it.

steps.title: Switched שבת and weekday clothes become impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן בן עמרם rules that if someone's שבת clothes were switched with his weekday clothes and he wore them, they become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן בן עמרם said: if his שבת clothes got switched with weekday clothes and he wore them, they became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruling of the same kind. A mix-up between two sets of clothes counts as not watching them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He thought he was wearing one set, but it was really the other. Because he was not paying attention to these particular clothes, they lose their pure status.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Amram said:
If his Shabbat clothes were switched
with weekday clothes, and he wore them,
they became impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling with the same idea as step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clothes worn by mistake in a mix-up become impure.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא declares switched bathhouse clothes impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק tells of two careful women whose clothes were switched in a bathhouse. רבי עקיבא declared the clothes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק said: there was a case of two women, both careful about purity, whose clothes got switched in the bathhouse. The case came before רבי עקיבא and he declared the clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case that backs up the ruling about switched clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both women were careful about purity, so neither one's clothes were impure on their own. Still, רבי עקיבא ruled them impure only because of the mix-up. That supports the idea that a mix-up alone causes impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Women who are careful about purity, like a חבר

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok said:
There was an incident with two women who were careful about purity
whose clothes were switched in the bathhouse,
and the case came before Rabbi Akiva,
and he declared them impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק: מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 6 with a story ruled on by רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: That a mix-up of clothes by itself makes them impure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A case of two careful women ruled on by רבי עקיבא

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: then grabbing the wrong bread would also make it impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא challenges these rulings: if a mix-up causes impurity, then grabbing barley bread instead of wheat bread should also make it impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא objected: if so, someone who reached into a basket for wheat bread and pulled out barley bread, would that bread also be impure?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא attacks the idea that a mix-up causes impurity by showing where it would lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If not knowing exactly which item you have makes it impure, then every small mistake, like grabbing the wrong loaf, would cause impurity. That seems too extreme, so the rule looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (now see where this leads)

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya objected to this:
But if so,
if someone stretched his hand into a basket
to take a loaf of wheat bread
and a loaf of barley bread came up in his hand,
would it also become impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule taught in steps 5 to 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a mix-up by itself causes impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: the rule would mean even grabbing the wrong loaf causes impurity, which seems absurd.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a barrel guarded as wine that turns out to be oil stays pure
steps.stepSummary: In case someone accepts that the bread would be impure, רבי אושעיא brings a ברייתא: a barrel guarded as wine that turns out to be oil is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say yes, the bread is impure, but a ברייתא teaches: if someone guards a barrel thinking it is wine and it turns out to be oil, it is pure and does not make others impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The objection is made stronger. In case someone 'bites the bullet' about the bread, a ברייתא is brought showing that a mix-up does not cause impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person was wrong about what was in the barrel, just like the clothes mix-up. Yet the ברייתא says the barrel stays pure. That seems to show a mistake about the item's identity does not make it impure.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say, yes, that is so
One who guards (to keep it pure)
Pure, so it does not pass on impurity

phrases.english: And if you would say, yes, it is so,
but wasn't it taught in a baraita:
One who guards a barrel
on the assumption that it is of wine,
and it turns out to be of oil,
it is pure, and does not make others impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבי אושעיא's objection in step 8 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That a mistake about which item one has does not cause impurity
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a barrel guarded as wine that turned out to be oil
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of רבי יונתן בן עמרם and רבי עקיבא (steps 6-7) that a mix-up by itself makes an item impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The barrel was guarded under a mistaken identity (wine that turned out to be oil), yet the ברייתא rules it טהורה מלטמא. So a mistake about identity should not cause impurity.

steps.title: But the same ברייתא forbids eating the oil, so why?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof: the end of that same ברייתא says the barrel is forbidden to eat. That shows the guarding was not fully good, so why would that be?
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your reasoning, read the end of the ברייתא: 'and it is forbidden to eat.' Why?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא weakens רבי אושעיא's proof by pointing to the end of the same ברייתא. It ends with a question, setting up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mistake did no harm at all, the oil should be allowed to eat. Since the ברייתא forbids eating it, the mistake must matter somehow. So the ברייתא does not clearly prove that a mix-up has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Read the end of the same source

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא contradicts itself. It says two different things: the barrel does not pass on impurity, yet it may not be eaten. The גמרא is about to explain how both can be true.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
read the end of that baraita:
"and it is forbidden to be eaten."
Why?
phrases.notes: If the mistake did no harm, eating it should be fine. The answer comes next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the proof from the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the first part of the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The end of the ברייתא forbids eating, which shows the mistake does affect the barrel. So the ברייתא cannot simply prove that a mix-up has no effect.

steps.title: He guarded it from impurity but not from disqualification
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains the end of the ברייתא. The owner guarded the barrel only from things that make it טמא, not from things that make it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: this is a case where the person says, 'I guarded it from things that make it impure, but not from things that disqualify it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the push-back from step 10, which asked why the barrel is forbidden to eat if the guarding worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of damage: being made טמא, which can spread to other things, and being made פסול, which only ruins the item itself. The owner watched for the first level but not the second. So the oil stays pure and cannot spread impurity, but it may not be eaten in case it became פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: in a case where he says
makes something impure (impurity that can spread)
disqualifies (makes it unusable, but it cannot spread impurity)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is a case where he says: I guarded it
phrases.notes: 'It' means the barrel from the ברייתא in step 9.

phrases.english: from something that makes it impure
but not from something that disqualifies it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push-back of step 10 and so rescues רבי אושעיא's proof from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the guarding covered one level of impurity but not the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the barrel is forbidden to eat, the guarding must have failed completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: The guarding worked against impurity that spreads, which keeps it טהור, but not against פסול, which is why it is forbidden to eat.

steps.title: Can someone guard only halfway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי ירמיה's answer: is it really possible to guard something from only one kind of impurity?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there such a thing as guarding halfway?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea behind רבי ירמיה's answer. This sets up a proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Guarding seems to be an all-or-nothing act: either you watched the item or you did not. The question is whether a person's attention can count for one level of impurity and not for another.

keyTerms.meaning: and is there really such a thing?

phrases.english: And is there such a thing as guarding halfway?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the idea behind רבי ירמיה's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that someone can guard from טומאה but not from פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Guarding seems to be one single act of paying attention, so it is hard to see how it could cover only part of the impurity.

steps.title: The basket and the shovel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and brings a ברייתא. A man paid attention to a basket but not to the shovel inside it, so the basket stays pure and the shovel becomes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. It was taught in a ברייתא: a man reached his hand into a basket. The basket was on his shoulder and a shovel was inside it. He was paying attention to the basket but not to the shovel. The basket is pure and the shovel is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that guarding can cover only part of what is in front of a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the guarding is split between two objects: the basket was guarded and the shovel was not. The next steps will test this ברייתא until it supports guarding split between two levels of impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: he had in mind, he was paying attention

phrases.english: Yes, and it was taught in a ברייתא:
If he stretched his hand into a basket,
and the basket was on his shoulder,
and the shovel was inside the basket,
and his mind was on the basket,
but his mind was not on the shovel —
the basket is pure and the shovel is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a basket that was guarded and a shovel inside it that was not.

steps.title: Shouldn't the shovel make the basket impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the shovel is impure and sitting inside the basket, why doesn't it make the basket impure too?
steps.simpleTranslation: The basket is pure? Let the shovel make the basket impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the ברייתא it just brought by asking how the basket can stay pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impure shovel is touching the basket. Normally that kind of contact should spread the impurity, so calling the basket pure needs an explanation.

phrases.english: The basket is pure?
Let the shovel make the basket impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in the ברייתא of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the basket stays טהור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An impure shovel touching the basket should pass its impurity on to the basket.

steps.title: A vessel does not make another vessel impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a rule: one vessel cannot make another vessel impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A vessel does not make a vessel impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14 with a known rule about impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the shovel and the basket are vessels. Because a vessel cannot pass impurity to another vessel, the basket stays pure even though the shovel is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: one vessel does not make another vessel impure

phrases.english: A vessel does not make a vessel impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A known rule of impurity is applied.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The impure shovel should make the basket impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vessel cannot make another vessel impure, so the basket stays טהור.

steps.title: Shouldn't the shovel make the food in the basket impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: even if the basket stays pure, the impure shovel should make the food inside the basket impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it make impure what is inside the basket!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second question on the ברייתא, this time about the food in the basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 15 only protects vessels. Food is not a vessel, so the impure shovel should make it impure, yet the ברייתא does not say so.

phrases.english: Then let it make impure what is in the basket!
phrases.notes: He means the food in the basket, like the figs. Food is not a vessel, so the rule from step 15 does not protect it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 15 and points out what that rule does not cover.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of step 13, which treats the contents of the basket as unaffected.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food can become impure from a vessel, so an impure shovel should make the food impure.

steps.title: רבינא: The shovel was guarded halfway
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the shovel was guarded from impurity that spreads, but not from things that disqualify it. So it is called impure, but it cannot pass impurity to the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: this is a case where he says, 'I guarded it from things that make it impure, but not from things that disqualify it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question from step 16. His answer also proves that guarding halfway is possible, which was the question in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shovel was only exposed to things that make it פסול, so it cannot spread impurity to the food. This is exactly the kind of half-guarding that רבי ירמיה described, so his answer in step 11 now stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Guarding can be partial. A person can protect an item from impurity that spreads while not protecting it from being disqualified. The item is then called impure but cannot make other things impure.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
It is a case where he says: I guarded it
from something that makes it impure
but not from something that disqualifies it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16. In doing so, it confirms that guarding halfway is possible, which answers step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the shovel was guarded halfway.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An impure shovel must make the food in the basket impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shovel is only פסול, which is why the ברייתא calls it impure, and it cannot spread impurity to the food. So guarding halfway exists.

steps.title: The original difficulty comes back
steps.stepSummary: Now that רבי ירמיה's answer holds up, the barrel proof stands. So רבי אושעיא's challenge to רבי יונתן בן עמרם and רבי עקיבא is a difficulty again.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי אושעיא's challenge from steps 8-9. The side discussion has been settled, and the original problem is back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The barrel ברייתא shows that guarding something under a mistaken identity, wine that turned out to be oil, still keeps it pure. That goes against the rulings in steps 6-7, which said a mix-up of clothes makes them impure.
steps.confusionAlert: The difficulty here is not about the basket or the shovel. It goes back to the switched clothes in steps 6-7 and the wine-and-oil barrel in step 9.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult?
phrases.notes: He means: either way, the barrel case still clashes with the rulings about the switched clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion that ended in step 17 and goes back to the challenge of steps 8-9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of רבי יונתן בן עמרם and רבי עקיבא that a mix-up in guarding makes clothes impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The barrel ברייתא, now defended by רבי ירמיה, shows that guarding under a mistaken identity still keeps an item pure.

steps.title: First story: the garment and the נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה raises another challenge. A woman wove a garment while pure but did not plan to guard it. Under questioning it came out that a נדה helped pull the rope, and רבי ישמעאל praised the חכמים' rule about guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה brought another challenge. A woman came to רבי ישמעאל and said: 'I wove this garment while I was pure, but I did not plan to guard it.' As he questioned her, she said: 'A נדה pulled the rope with me.' רבי ישמעאל said: 'How great are the words of the חכמים! If you mean to guard it, it is pure. If you don't, it is impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge from רבה בר אבוה, using a story about רבי ישמעאל. The woman did not plan to guard her garment, and in the end it really had become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman thought nothing impure had touched the garment. Questioning showed that a נדה had moved it, which makes it impure. רבי ישמעאל saw this as proof of the חכמים' rule: if you don't intend to guard an item, treat it as impure, because things happen that you don't notice.

keyTerms.meaning: to guard it in a state of purity
a woman who is impure from her period

phrases.english: And Rabba bar Avuh raised a further objection:
There was an incident with a certain woman
who came before Rabbi Yishmael,
and said to him: Rabbi,
I wove this garment in purity,
but I did not have it in mind to guard it in purity.
And in the course of the questioning
that Rabbi Yishmael was doing with her,
she said to him: Rabbi,
a menstruating woman pulled the rope with me.
phrases.notes: When a נדה moves the garment, it becomes impure even though she may not have touched it directly.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
How great are the words of the Sages,
who used to say:
if he has it in mind to guard it, it is pure;
if he does not have it in mind to guard it, it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 18 restates the first difficulty, רבה בר אבוה adds a further challenge against the same rulings. Steps 22-23 explain how those rulings hold up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of רבי יונתן בן עמרם and רבי עקיבא (steps 6-7) that a mix-up while guarding makes an item impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל's rule makes the lack of intent to guard the thing that makes an item impure. This sets up an inference that whoever did intend to guard keeps the item pure.

steps.title: Second story: the cloth and the snapped thread
steps.stepSummary: A second woman wove a cloth while pure but did not plan to guard it. Under questioning she said a thread snapped and she tied it with her mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another woman came to רבי ישמעאל and said: 'I wove this cloth while I was pure, but I did not plan to guard it.' As he questioned her, she said: 'A thread snapped, and I tied it with my mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge goes on with a second, similar story. Again a woman who did not plan to guard her item finds out that something happened to it which she had not noticed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying the thread with her mouth wet it with saliva. Wet things become impure much more easily. So without careful guarding, the cloth could easily have become impure without her knowing.

phrases.english: Another incident with a certain woman
who came before Rabbi Yishmael;
she said to him: Rabbi,
I wove this cloth in purity,
but I did not have it in mind to guard it.
And in the course of the questioning
that Rabbi Yishmael was doing with her,
she said to him: Rabbi,
a thread of mine snapped
and I tied it with my mouth.
phrases.notes: Her saliva made the thread wet, and wet things pick up impurity easily.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that adds to the first one inside the same challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second case strengthens the pattern: without the intent to guard, an item ends up impure.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל repeats the rule of guarding
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל again praises the חכמים' rule: if you mean to guard it, it is pure; if not, it is impure. This is the line the challenge depends on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: 'How great are the words of the חכמים! If you mean to guard it, it is pure. If you don't, it is impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי ישמעאל's statement for the second story. This rule is the heart of רבה בר אבוה's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends only on whether the person intended to guard the item. That suggests that someone who did plan to guard it keeps it pure, even if they made a mistake along the way. This is what puts pressure on the view being discussed.
steps.whatToRemember: The key test here is intention. If you mean to guard an item, it stays pure. If you don't, it is treated as impure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
How great are the words of the Sages,
who used to say:
if he has it in mind to guard it, it is pure;
if he does not have it in mind to guard it, it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the second story with the same rule, which gives the challenge its force.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a mistake made while guarding counts as taking one's mind off the item
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If intent to guard is the only test, then someone who intended to guard should keep the item pure, even if they were mistaken.

steps.title: How רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's view fits the two wives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new question. It says רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's view is easy to explain: each wife assumes her friend is married to an עם הארץ, so she stops caring about her garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי אלעזר בר צדוק it works: each wife says, 'My friend is the wife of an עם הארץ,' and she takes her mind off her garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty from steps 18-21 by showing that the switched-garments case involves a real lapse of attention. This is also a setup line: after explaining this case and the next one, it will challenge רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's case in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of the two wives of חברים whose garments got switched, each woman thinks the garment she now has belongs to an עם הארץ's wife. So she stops watching it, and that is real היסח הדעת. This explains why the garments in רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's story were ruled impure, and it prepares an 'אלא' question on רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: someone not careful about purity laws
she takes her mind off it

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא' does not finish the question. It is the first half; the hard part comes in step 24 ('אלא לרבי יונתן בן אלעזר'), which is about the fallen shawl and not about this case.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok,
each and every one says:
phrases.notes: 'Each one' means each of the two wives of חברים whose garments got switched.

phrases.english: my friend is the wife of an am ha'aretz,
and she takes her mind off it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of steps 18-21 for רבי עקיבא's switched-garments case: unlike the barrel, here the mistake causes real היסח הדעת. It also begins a 'בשלמא' setup that ends with the challenge to רבי יונתן בן אלעזר in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's ruling about the fallen shawl handed back by a friend (step 5); the challenge comes in step 24
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First it shows that the switched-clothes cases work through a real היסח הדעת. That sets up the question on רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's case, where the owner never lost track of his shawl.

steps.title: The שבת clothes case is also easy to explain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן בן עמרם's case of switched שבת and weekday clothes fits the logic: a person guards שבת clothes extra carefully, so when he thinks they are weekday clothes he drops that extra care.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יונתן בן עמרם too it makes sense: since a person guards שבת clothes more carefully, he takes his mind off them when he thinks they are weekday clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still setting up its question. It shows that a second case, רבי יונתן בן עמרם's switched clothes, is also easy to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת clothes usually get a higher level of guarding. If someone mistakes them for weekday clothes, he guards them less, and that drop in attention is a real היסח הדעת. So this case fits the rule, which sets up the hard case in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarding, watching over something so it stays טהור
He takes his mind off it (היסח הדעת)

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yonatan ben Amram too,
phrases.notes: His case is the person who mixed up his שבת clothes with his weekday clothes.

phrases.english: since Shabbat clothes,
he guards them more carefully,
he takes his mind off them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 22: רבי יונתן בן עמרם's switched-clothes case (step 6) also survives the difficulty of steps 18-21, because thinking they are weekday clothes drops the extra care, which is real היסח הדעת.
steps.kashyaTarget: Prepares the challenge against רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By showing two cases are easy, the גמרא makes the third case stand out as the hard one.

steps.title: Why can't he guard the garment in his friend's hand?
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's case, a friend picks up the owner's fallen garment. The גמרא asks: the owner can keep guarding it while the friend holds it, so why should it be impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יונתן בן אלעזר, let him guard the garment while it is in his friend's hand!
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the real challenge. In רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's case the owner never lost track of his garment, so why does it count as a lapse in attention?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first two cases, the owner truly changed how he related to the garment: he didn't know it was his, or he thought it was less special. Here he knows exactly where it is, in his friend's hand. So there seems to be no reason to call this היסח הדעת.

keyTerms.meaning: But, rather; here it turns to the hard case

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar,
phrases.notes: His case is the man whose cloak fell, and his friend picked it up for him.

phrases.english: let him guard them
in his friend's hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two easy cases, the גמרא challenges the third.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's ruling that the garment picked up by a friend is impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner knows where his garment is and can still watch it, so there should be no היסח הדעת and no impurity.

steps.title: A person does not guard what is in someone else's hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that there is a חזקה: people don't really guard something while another person is holding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is a presumption that a person does not guard what is in his friend's hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. We assume that once an item is in someone else's hands, the owner stops watching it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not about this particular man but about how people normally act. When a friend holds your item, you naturally leave the watching to him. So even if the owner could guard it, we assume he didn't, and that counts as היסח הדעת.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption: what we assume people normally do
What is in his friend's hand

steps.whyThisMatters: This חזקה explains רבי יונתן בן אלעזר's ruling. The next steps test whether it is really true.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is a presumption: a person does not guard
what is in his friend's hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חֲזָקָה, אֵין אָדָם מְשַׁמֵּר מַה שֶּׁבְּיַד חֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יונתן בן אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general presumption about how people behave
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner could keep guarding the garment in his friend's hand, so it should stay pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: We assume people don't guard what someone else is holding, so there is היסח הדעת and the garment is impure.

steps.title: Can a person really not guard what another holds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's חזקה: is it really true that a person cannot guard something in another person's hand?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does he not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer with one short word. It is setting up a challenge that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וְלֹא?" is short for "Is it really true that a person does not guard what is in his friend's hand?" The question suggests there is a source showing that people do guard such things. The proof itself comes in the following text.

keyTerms.meaning: "And not?": a short way of asking "Is that really so?"

phrases.english: And does he not?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: is it really true that he doesn't guard it? A proof against this is coming next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the חזקה that רבי יוחנן just gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's חזקה that a person does not guard what is in his friend's hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doubts the assumption and sets up a source suggesting a person can guard an item someone else is holding.
